Cardio-Audio-Synchrnoization Task in FND

Author

Natascha Stoffel

Published

August 26, 2026

Information on the Data

BASEC registration number : 2023-0469

Study Visit “Interoception” conducted between 18.10.2023 - 4.9.2024, with completed N=92 participants. N = 4 did not start/ finish the CAS thus no data were available due to high symptoms. N =2 had to be excluded for low EEG quality, N = 7 had to be excluded due to technical errors in the algorithm of R-peak detection and stimulus presentation, and N = 1 because they fell asleep during the task. Following analysis was thus conducted with a final sample size of N = 78 participants.

In this analysis we will be looking at the RedCap data that is downloaded from the redcapmed.unifr.ch server, with project number PID 121, named “Interoception”

Also, we will do further analysis of extracted EEG data. Meaning, the EEG data has been processed locally in Cartool and Fieldtrip (calculating electrodes cluster intervals of differences between conditions / groups). For significant clusters, mean cluster were extracted for the identified interval to further run statistics and correlation with other clinical/interoceptive data.

Secondly, EEG analysis included whole-scalp analysis in RAGU to derive main and interaction effects of the 2x2 factor structure of the task (group: FND vs HC and condition: interoceptive vs exteroceptive predictive coding).

# define medication as it interstes us, that have an effect on the BRAIN (which is all psychotropic medication, benzos, morphiom/opiod pain killers and antiepileitc medication)
df <- Data.CRF %>%
  mutate(medication_brain = dplyr::if_else(psychotropic_medication == 1 | sleep_benzo == 1 | pain_antiepi == 1 | pain_morph_opio == 1, 1, 0))  # 1=yes so if there is a yes in any of the different medication categories, there will be a 1 in medication_brain

df <- df %>%
  mutate(medication_brain = if_else(is.na(medication_brain), 0, medication_brain)) # assign a 0 to missing values

# create a common depression-anxiety variable as it highly correlates (and to not mess with the models)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(anx_dep_SUM = stai_t + bdi)# create one variable for the trait anxiety and depression to use as one variable in the model

#making sure everything is stored as the correct variable

df$contraception <- as.factor(df$contraception)

df$ias <- as.numeric(df$ias)
df$maia_total <- as.numeric(df$maia_total)
df$rrst_sensitivity <- as.numeric(df$rrst_sensitivity)
df$hbt_accuracy_mean <- as.numeric(df$hbt_accuracy_mean)

# define required subgroups

df_male <- df[df$sex == "2", ]

1.2 Group differences

# calculation of cohens d for variable of interest
# Define the function
calculate_cohens_d <- function(data, variable, group_var, group1, group2) {
  # Subset the data for each group
  group1_data <- data[[variable]][data[[group_var]] == group1]
  group2_data <- data[[variable]][data[[group_var]] == group2]
  
  # Calculate means and standard deviations
  mean1 <- mean(group1_data, na.rm = TRUE)
  mean2 <- mean(group2_data, na.rm = TRUE)
  sd1 <- sd(group1_data, na.rm = TRUE)
  sd2 <- sd(group2_data, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Calculate sample sizes
  n1 <- sum(!is.na(group1_data))
  n2 <- sum(!is.na(group2_data))
  
  # Calculate pooled standard deviation
  sd_pooled <- sqrt(((n1 - 1) * sd1^2 + (n2 - 1) * sd2^2) / (n1 + n2 - 2))
  
  # Calculate Cohen's d
  cohens_d <- (mean1 - mean2) / sd_pooled
  
  # Return Cohen's d
  return(cohens_d)
}

# Calculate Cohen's d for variables of differences
cohens_d_bdi <- calculate_cohens_d(df, "bdi", "group", 1, 0) # group 1=FND, group=0 HC
print(cohens_d_bdi)

2.1 Condition difference in HC: Effect Size

# New function for effect size for WITHIN group difference (isntead of between group as before)

calculate_cohens_d_paired <- function(data,  variable1, variable2,group_var,group) {
  # Subset data for the selected group
  variable1_data <- data[[variable1]][data[[group_var]] == group]
  variable2_data <- data[[variable2]][data[[group_var]] == group]

  # Keep only complete pairs
  complete_cases <- !is.na(variable1_data) & !is.na(variable2_data)

  variable1_data <- variable1_data[complete_cases]
  variable2_data <- variable2_data[complete_cases]

  # Calculate within-person differences
  differences <- variable1_data - variable2_data

  # Calculate Cohen's d for paired data
  cohens_d <- mean(differences) / sd(differences)
  cohens_d}

cohens_d_Ccluster_120 <- calculate_cohens_d_paired(df,"Ccluster_120_synch", "Ccluster_120_asynch",  "group",  0)

# Perform correlation tests for the differences of synch-asynch with interoceptive scores
perform_correlation_tests <- function(variable, df) {
  x <- df[[variable]]
  if (!is.numeric(x)) return(NULL)

  tests <- list(
    IAS  = cor.test(x, df$ias, method = "pearson"),
    MAIA = cor.test(x, df$maia_total, method = "pearson"),
    RRST = cor.test(x, df$rrst_sensitivity, method = "pearson"),
    HBT  = cor.test(x, df$hbt_accuracy_mean, method = "pearson") )

  p_values <- sapply(tests, function(x) x$p.value)
  p_adjusted <- p.adjust(p_values, method = "fdr")

  results <- data.frame(
    Variable = variable,
    Comparison = names(p_values),
    Raw_p_value = p_values,
    Adjusted_p_value = p_adjusted )

  return(results)
}

# Perform tests for following variable
variables <- c("Ccluster_257")

all_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(variables, perform_correlation_tests, df))
